summary: YouTube temporarily demonetized SSSniperwolf (Alia Shelesh) after she posted an Instagram story showing the outside of fellow creator Jacksfilms' (Jack Douglass) home, which he called doxxing. The feud grew out of Douglass's long-running criticism of her reaction content for lacking credit and transformative commentary. Many fans felt YouTube's response was a slap on the wrist, especially since it referenced "both sides."
one_line: YouTube temporarily demonetized SSSniperwolf after she posted Jacksfilms' house on Instagram, reigniting debate over reaction content and creator conduct.
key_facts: Alia "SSSniperwolf" Shelesh is a YouTuber with over 34 million subscribers; Jack "Jacksfilms" Douglass has 4.9 million subscribers.

On Oct. 13, Shelesh posted an Instagram story asking "Should I go visit @Jacksfilms? He lives 5 mins away from my shoot," followed by a photo of the outside of Douglass' house captioned "Let's talk like adults."
Douglass was livestreaming on Twitch when the posts appeared and tweeted on Oct. 13: "Sssniperwolf just doxxed me on her IG. Creepy, gross, violating."
On Oct. 20, TeamYouTube confirmed Shelesh received "a temporary monetization suspension per Creator Responsibility policies."
YouTube's tweet also criticized "the behavior on both sides," which drew complaints that it implied Douglass shared responsibility.
Shelesh apologized on X to "Jacksfilm, YouTube, the entire creator community, and my incredible fans for not being a better example of conflict resolution."
After the apology, Shelesh posted new videos to YouTube with the comment sections disabled.
Douglass has made YouTube content since 2006, mainly comedy, and has criticized reaction content that he says fails fair use standards.
Douglass revived an old joke channel called JJJacksfilms and streamed on Twitch grading Shelesh's reaction content with a bingo game for viewers.
Shelesh has been a creator for roughly a decade on YouTube and TikTok, and her recent work is largely reaction content.
In 2016, the Fine Brothers attempted to copyright their "React" videos and met near unanimous criticism.
In August, Félix "xQc" Lengyel and other creators reacted to long-form content with little original input, reigniting the reaction content debate.
Public opinion was largely in favor of Douglass, and the demonetization was seen as a slap on the wrist.
